questions.text: Dominic. She's never once said that name to me. Sorry to keep asking — can you get me the rest of it, his surname?
questions.hint: Open Contacts and search for Dominic — his profile gives his full last name.

questions.text: Reyes. Okay. She wrote to that man about me, didn't she — can you tell me what the two of them were arranging?
questions.hint: Open Email and search for messages linked to Dominic. Open the email in Corinne's sent folder: the subject line perfectly sums up their conversation.

questions.text: She sent him my bank information. Like a work ticket. Please just say the number back to me — how much did I actually transfer her?
questions.hint: Open RevoBank and look in the transaction history for the money received from Sutton — the exact amount appears by clicking on the transfer line.

questions.text: I signed that transfer myself. I remember feeling generous about it... Could you find out how much more they were planning to get out of me?
questions.hint: Open WhatsApp and go to the conversation with Dominic to find the total amount he wants to reach. Then subtract what Sutton has already paid to find out how much more they're going to ask him for.

questions.text: Twenty-five more, on top. I keep thinking I can't have been the only one — could you find me the name of somebody else they took money from?
questions.hint: Open WhatsApp and scroll all the way up to the very first messages in the conversation with Dominic - right at the top, before anything else, they mention someone named Howard and a transfer.

questions.text: Howard Tillman. A real person, with a real life, who also doesn't know yet. Can you tell me how much she's taken in total, all of us added together?
questions.hint: Look in the Notes app for a locked note — the code is based on Corinne's date of birth, which you'll find in her contact profile.

questions.text: Twenty-three thousand. She sat at my table while that number was going up... Could you tell me where she actually worked before any of this?
questions.hint: Go to the Email app, open the side menu and go to the Trash. You'll find an official contract termination letter there that mentions the name of her former firm.

onboarding.text: Hey... My name's Sutton. I write software. I spend all day refusing to trust a system until the logs prove it out. I never once did that with her. I feel like an idiot.
onboarding.label: Sutton

onboarding.text: I met Corinne at a networking evening in Charlotte, back in the winter. She was starting a reforestation charity — the Piedmont Canopy Fund. In July I wired her the money myself. I was proud of it.
onboarding.label: Sutton & Corinne

onboarding.text: For about three weeks now she's been somewhere else. Short answers. My questions just slide off her. Then this morning Neil called me from Atlanta. He'd gone looking for the Fund's filings, and there aren't any.
onboarding.label: Corinne

onboarding.text: She left her phone on the table this morning. I haven't opened it. If I read it myself I'll find the version where she meant it... I've done that every night for weeks. Please, you look.
onboarding.label: Sutton

notes.title: Recipe — weeknight shakshuka
notes.body:
For two:
- 1 can crushed tomatoes
- 1 red bell pepper
- 1 onion
- 2 cloves of garlic
- 4 eggs
- Cumin, smoked paprika, a spoonful of harissa
- Feta and fresh coriander over the top

Onion, garlic and pepper go into the pan to start. Tomatoes and spices after that, then let it cook down for ten minutes. Make four hollows, crack an egg into each, lid on for 5-7 minutes. Pita alongside.

→ quick, and genuinely good. Mum would approve.
